advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace or drop the prose-phrasing assertions (`"does not invalidate"`, `"never echo or log"`) in favor of the canonical credential-reuse identifiers already asserted, to avoid coupling the test to wording.
evidence: assert "never echo or log" in guidance.lower()

Rule-5 litmus: an LLM is not a non-human consumer; a prose/heading grep that merely guards the author's wording is a change-detector, unlike the canonical `curl --netrc`/`.netrc`/`401` identifier greps in the same test which downstream grep/validators branch on.
advisory.finding: Two of the new assertions grep author prose phrasing (`"does not invalidate"` and `"never echo or log"`) rather than canonical command/identifier tokens; they would break on a behavior-preserving reword of the guidance, making them phrasing change-detectors. The adjacent canonical-token assertions (`git credential fill`, `curl --netrc`, `.netrc`, `401`) already anchor the same behavior, so the prose assertions add coupling without extra regression protection.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Change the AGENTS.md Gerrit example to keep the password off the curl command line (e.g. pipe a config via `curl -K -` / stdin, or write a temp `--netrc-file`) instead of `--user "$user:$pass"`.
evidence: AGENTS.md:58: `Never echo or log the credential response or password, and keep shell tracing disabled while using them.`
Passing secrets as argv exposes them to any local process able to read the process table (`ps -ef`, `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`); this is a concrete reachability path on shared/CI hosts, not speculation.
advisory.finding: The Gerrit credential-fetch snippet in AGENTS.md passes the retrieved password on the curl command line via `--user "$gerrit_user:$gerrit_password"`, which exposes the plaintext password in the process table (ps / /proc/<pid>/cmdline) to other local processes while the request runs — contradicting the same block's 'Never echo or log the credential' instruction.
scenarios: A Codex session runs on a shared or CI host where another process/user can enumerate the process table during the curl call.
Agents copy this prescribed pattern into scripts, propagating the argv-exposed-credential form.
advisory.suggested_fix:
Feed the credential to curl without placing it on argv, e.g.:
`printf 'user = "%s:%s"\n' "$gerrit_user" "$gerrit_password" | curl --fail --silent --show-error -K - https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/a/changes/`
so the password is read from stdin/config rather than the process table.
